events.title: The FBI’s Project Megiddo names the Black Hebrew Israelites
events.summary: On October 20, 1999 the FBI released Project Megiddo, a report that named followers of white supremacy, Christian Identity, the militia movement, the Black Hebrew Israelites and apocalyptic cults as potential terrorists who might turn violent at the new millennium.
account: Project Megiddo was researched and written by the Federal Bureau of Investigation under Director Louis Freeh and released on October 20, 1999. Its stated purpose was to warn domestic law enforcement of “the potential for extremist criminal activity in the United States by individuals or domestic groups who attach special significance to the year 2000.” It named the Black Hebrew Israelites among the movements whose followers might become violent in reaction to the new millennium, alongside white supremacists, Christian Identity, the militia movement and apocalyptic cults.

The report said “violent radical fringe members” of the Black Hebrew Israelite movement hold beliefs that “bear a striking resemblance to the Christian Identity theology practiced by many white supremacists.”

The report drew criticism at the time: Insight on the News called it “a polemic presented as a threat report” in which the FBI “has targeted religious groups.” On January 6, 2000, asked why the predicted acts of terror had not happened, Attorney General Janet Reno answered that “the nice answer would be that there was no threat.”

points: The secret plots against Israel begin with defamation of character, and when defamation does not work, then comes martyrdom: so it was when the adversaries hindered the building of the temple “by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions.” Project Megiddo is one link in that chain of events: it talks about the plans of America.
teaching.quote: They got something called Project Megiddo, y'all can look that up when you want, when you get a chance. Talks about the plans of America.

scriptures.why: Read at the opening of the class: the adversaries hindered the building of the temple with secret plots, popular persuasions and commotions, as they work to hinder the building of the nation of Israel today, beginning with defamation.

answer.why: Read by the class with this report: “by their secret plots, and popular persuasions and commotions, they hindered the finishing of the building.” The work of rebuilding Israel was spoken against and hindered before; a government report naming the people as a threat is the same pattern.
“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones… that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” Counsel taken against a hidden people is foretold.
Christ himself was charged as a danger to the state: “We found this fellow perverting the nation.” What was said of him is said of his people.

events.title: The Southern Poverty Law Center lists Israel United in Christ as a hate group

date.text: First in the report published February 4, 2016 (for 2015); listed for 2015–2018, 2021 and 2022

events.summary: The Southern Poverty Law Center (SPLC) listed Israel United in Christ among active hate groups in its annual reports for 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2021 and 2022; IUIC denies it is a hate group.
account: The SPLC, a nonprofit legal advocacy organization in Montgomery, Alabama, has published an annual census of hate groups since 1990. Its report “Active Hate Groups in the United States in 2015,” published February 4, 2016, included Israel United in Christ among its black separatist and black nationalist groups, and IUIC appears in the SPLC’s lists for 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2021 and 2022. In 2008 the SPLC had written that “the extremist fringe of the Hebrew Israelite movement” had a Black supremacist outlook, while also writing that “most Hebrew Israelites are neither explicitly racist nor anti-Semitic and do not advocate violence.”

In 2019 Heidi Beirich of the SPLC told the BBC that the center lists IUIC as a “black nationalist hate group” and “racist”: “racist against white people, racist against Jews,” and “incredibly homophobic, as well.” The Oklahoman reported in 2022 that the SPLC designated IUIC a hate group “notably due to what the nonprofit law center described as the group’s anti-white, anti-Semitic and anti-LGBTQ messaging,” and placed it among groups espousing “Radical Hebrew Israelites” ideology.

IUIC denies that it is a hate group. It told the BBC that “at no point do we teach against the laws of the land or authorities.” Bishop Kani told The Oklahoman the group had been “mislabeled”: “We don’t promote violence, we’re not out there looking to harm people… they translate when we talk as hate because we’re trying to empower ourselves.” Many of IUIC’s videos open with the disclaimer “We are not a hate group,” and its website tells members to notify the authorities of any plot to cause harm or break the laws of the land.

points: Once a group is put on the hate list, it becomes a target: every IUIC branch is listed with its address and phone number, so that somebody will come in and do something. That is why the schools keep security.
teaching.quote: They're trying to stir people up against us.

points: We are not a hate group, we are not affiliated with any other Israelite group, and we do not advocate or condone violence against any race, ethnicity or gender; anyone who hears of a plot to harm anyone or break the laws of the land must report it. Satan is trying to paint Israel as hateful and violent, so the brothers must not answer evil with evil: even when we are right, an altercation makes us wrong. Christ had all power and did not have to prove anything; that is not softness.
teaching.quote: Satan trying to paint our image of the Israelites of us being hateful

answer.why: The classes’ first answer: “Recompense to no man evil for evil… If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men. Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves… Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.” IUIC’s own disclaimer rests on this.
“And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.” Read with Romans 12 in the class on this charge.
Cited by IUIC’s website, as the CDAMM entry records, for telling members to report any plot to harm or to break the law: a witness who does not utter it “shall bear his iniquity.”
Also cited by IUIC’s website: “Let every soul be subject unto the higher powers.” A people taught this is not teaching against the laws of the land.
“If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you… If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you.” The ring: what was done to Christ is done to his people.
“If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household?” Christ was given an evil name first.

events.title: Kendrick Lamar’s DAMN. carries the Israelite message, and is spoken against
events.summary: Kendrick Lamar’s album DAMN., released April 14, 2017, carried a voicemail from his cousin Carl Duckworth, a Hebrew Israelite, reading Deuteronomy 28:28 and saying the so-called Blacks, Hispanics and Native American Indians are the true children of Israel; the album won the 2018 Pulitzer Prize for Music.
account: DAMN., Kendrick Lamar’s fourth studio album, was released on April 14, 2017. The song “Fear” opens with a voicemail from Lamar’s cousin Karni Israel Duckworth (then Carl Duckworth), a member of the Black Hebrew Israelites, reciting Deuteronomy 28:28. In a second voicemail at the end of the song he says: “The so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native American Indians are the true children of Israel. We are the Israelites, according to the Bible. The children of Israel. He’s gonna punish us for our iniquities, for our disobedience because we chose to follow other gods.” On “Yah” Lamar says, “I’m an Israelite, don’t call me Black no more.”

The album debuted at the top of the Billboard 200 with 603,000 album-equivalent units in its first week and earned Lamar the 2018 Pulitzer Prize for Music, the first time the prize went to an artist outside classical music and jazz. The Washington Post wrote in January 2019 that Israel United in Christ had been “thrust into the spotlight after rap superstar Kendrick Lamar featured snippets of his cousin, one of its members, preaching on his Pulitzer Prize-winning album.”

Commentary on the album spoke against the message. As played and read in the class of April 27, 2017, a video review called the idea that slavery, genocide and Jim Crow came as divine punishment “stupid,” “bordering on self-hatred,” and “the exact opposite of being conscious”; a Christian blog read in the same class said the album was “littered with Hebrew Israelite references and theology” and predicted Lamar would lead young men away from Christ.

points: The reviewer called it depression and self-hatred to lay our woes at God’s feet. Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad: we are mad because of what we see our people go through, and the Lord said he would smite us with madness. That does not make us want to die; we throw ourselves on the mercy of the Lord to get us out of here.

They wanted him to be conscious only to a point, to deal with the economy and imprisonment but never delve into the Bible. The Bible has always been the problem for them. The brief message he put out reached millions, and that is the fear.
teaching.quote: The white man knows the power is in the book and that's where the fear comes in

points: The article said the Hebrew Israelite camps “passionately hate one another.” The law says otherwise: thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart, and whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer. Israelite camps must not hate one another.

The article called keeping the law a heresy. Blessed are they that do his commandments, and here are they that keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus: that is not leaving Christ, it is going to Christ. If that is heresy, we are on the right track.
Israel’s bondage in the transatlantic slave trade is what Luke 21:24 foretold: led away captive into all nations until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

scriptures.why: Answer to the charge of “depression”: oppression maketh a wise man mad.
The verse Carl Duckworth read on the album: the madness of seeing what our people go through is the curse foretold.
Read to the camps who hate one another: thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart.
Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer.
Against the charge that keeping the law is heresy: blessed are they that do his commandments.
The saints keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus: keeping the law is going to Christ.
Read for the claim that the transatlantic slave trade fell on the true Israelites: led away captive into all nations.

answer.why: The class’s first answer to “self-hatred” and “depression”: “Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad.” Knowing the cause of the suffering is wisdom, not hatred of self.
“The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.” The verse on the album is the Lord’s own word that the suffering would come for disobedience.
Answer to “heretical”: “Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life.”
“Here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” Law and Christ together, as the class read it.
Paul answered the same charge: “after the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets.”

events.title: The FBI’s “Black Identity Extremists” designation

date.text: Report dated August 3, 2017; designation used until July 2019

events.summary: From August 2017 to July 2019 the FBI used the designation “Black Identity Extremists,” first in a counterterrorism report dated August 3, 2017 sent to thousands of police departments; critics said it described a movement that did not exist.
account: “Black Identity Extremists” first appeared in an FBI counterterrorism report dated August 3, 2017 and sent to thousands of American police departments, describing safety concerns about allegedly violent African-American activists. Foreign Policy published the leaked report in October 2017; it stated that “[t]he FBI assesses it is very likely Black Identity Extremist perceptions of police brutality against African Americans spurred an increase in premeditated, retaliatory lethal violence against law enforcement.” Former government officials and legal experts said the term described a movement that did not exist.

In November 2017 the National Organization of Black Law Enforcement Executives called the designation “ill advised,” and in March 2018 it was discussed in the Congressional Black Caucus. Civil liberties groups warned it would treat Black activism as equivalent to white supremacist violence. The FBI dropped the term in July 2019, merging several categories under “racially motivated violent extremism”; according to the ACLU, leaked documents showed a program called IRON FIST continued to investigate Black activists.

points: Representative Karen Bass pressed the Attorney General on the report, Black Identity Extremists likely motivated to target law enforcement officers, and showed that the organizations it named were from decades ago and that no such group exists. When it was proved there was no Black identity extremist group, they set out to manufacture one: the Jersey City attack was made to serve that purpose.
teaching.quote: Esau said well there isn't one we got embarrassed les manufacture one

points: People think they are mocking us, but they are mocking the Lord, because we come with the words of the Lord: whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

source.title: #IUIC | GOD & THE IRON FIST | BLACK IDENTITY EXTREMIST | PART 2

points: No one can explain what a Black identity extremist is. It is not about any organization terrorizing society; it is about Black people coming together and keeping the commandments, which Hoover called the most serious threat. They are setting laws in place to come after the Israelites, the followers of Christ.

events.title: SPLC Hatewatch writes against IUIC’s mission to Liberia
events.summary: On April 11, 2018 the SPLC’s Hatewatch attacked Israel United in Christ’s mission to Liberia because Bishop Nathanyel held a Bible study with Joshua Milton Blahyi, the former warlord “General Butt Naked,” who had renounced his killings and become an evangelist.
account: The SPLC’s Hatewatch article of April 11, 2018, “Courting Butt Naked,” described IUIC as a Black Hebrew Israelite group based in the Bronx that thinks white people are “the devil,” Jews “fake Jews” and LGBT people “sinners,” and said it had “no qualms about recruiting a cannibal who led a child army.” It reported that IUIC travelled to Liberia, preaching at a Liberian church, on the street and on local radio, and that Bishop Nathanyel Ben Israel led a Bible study with Joshua Milton Blahyi, known as General Butt Naked.

By the article’s own account, Blahyi had fought in Liberia’s civil war, which began in 1989, and told the 2008 Truth and Reconciliation Commission he took part in at least 20,000 killings; he said a vision ended his life of bloodshed and led to his conversion, and he now preaches as “Blahyi the Evangelist” and tries to reach the child soldiers he left behind. The SPLC wrote that IUIC saw him as an opportunity to push its outreach into Africa “past deeds be damned,” quoting a member who told him: “you can reach a lot of people… but you gotta take them the true gospel.”

answer.why: The same charge was laid against Christ: “This man receiveth sinners, and eateth with them.” Teaching a sinner who has turned from his deeds is the work of the gospel, not a crime.
“They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick… I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” IUIC teaches the gospel of repentance from sin.

“They say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.” The ring again: what was said of Christ is said of those who follow him.

events.title: The murder of Joy Morgan, and the charges laid against the church

date.text: Last seen December 26, 2018; conviction August 5, 2019; inquest 2021

events.summary: Joy Morgan, a 20-year-old midwifery student and member of IUIC’s UK branch, was murdered after a church celebration on December 26, 2018; fellow member Shohfah-El Israel was convicted on August 5, 2019, and coverage of the case carried her family’s and the SPLC’s charges against the church, which IUIC denied.
account: Joy Morgan, born February 12, 1998, was a midwifery student at the University of Hertfordshire. She joined the UK branch of Israel United in Christ in Ilford, east London, in January 2016, ran its children’s group, and two weeks before she went missing said in a video, “IUIC is my family and like the best family that I’ve ever had.” She was last seen alive on December 26, 2018 at a church celebration in Ilford. She was reported missing on February 7, 2019, after her housemates had not seen her since Christmas.

Police arrested fellow member Shohfah-El Israel (born Ajibola Shogbamimu) on February 9, 2019 on the M25; he was charged with murder on February 27. He admitted spending two nights alone with her at his Cricklewood flat, which broke the church’s rule against women being alone with men other than their husbands. A jury at Reading Crown Court convicted him on August 5, 2019, and he was sentenced to life with a minimum of 17 years; he refused to say where her body was. Her remains were found in woodland near Stevenage in October 2019. A 2021 coroner’s inquest could not establish how she died.

The coverage carried charges against the church. Her mother Carol said her daughter had been turned into a racist by the church and called it a cult, and her family said she had grown distant and called her mixed-race younger sister a “demon” and a “white devil.” Former members told the BBC of harsh discipline and of being told to cut off unbelieving family. The prosecutor described a strict hierarchy in which women had no rank. The SPLC described IUIC as a “hate group” and “a black nationalist group.”

IUIC denied these claims. It told the BBC that former members who speak against it are “disgruntled,” that claims it encourages members to cut off their families are “lies,” and that “at no point do we teach against the laws of the land or authorities.” The church described Shohfah-El Israel as an “enthusiastic” member and said he had once been demoted from the rank of soldier over his behaviour. Evidence given at the trial indicated that Joy Morgan had a good relationship with the church and its congregants, and police found no reliable indication that she wanted to leave it.

points: Years after her death, other camps print Joy Morgan’s picture and teach in the street that IUIC had something to do with her death, all the way over in England, while they say nothing of a 13-year-old girl abused by a man who called himself a Hebrew Israelite. All Israelite groups are not the same, and IUIC has no affiliation with those groups.
So the chief priests and Pharisees followed Christ’s camp and sought to lay hands on him, but feared the multitude: digging into a member’s personal life is to turn the multitude against us.

points: When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest. Joy Morgan is at rest now: the police did their investigation and found the person who caused her harm. Holding up her picture in the street to incite the public against the assembly breaks the law of God.

To the word “cult”: the apostles were called a “sect,” and “every where it is spoken against.” The classes have read Acts 24:5, 24:14 and 28:22 against the name cult.

events.title: The Lincoln Memorial confrontation, and the coverage that followed
events.summary: On January 18, 2019, at the Lincoln Memorial, a small group of Hebrew Israelite street preachers, identified as members of the House of Israel, taunted passers-by before the viral encounter between Covington Catholic students and the Omaha elder Nathan Phillips; the coverage brought the whole movement, and IUIC by name, into the national spotlight.
account: On January 18, 2019 the Indigenous Peoples March and the March for Life met on the Plaza of the Lincoln Memorial. Before Covington Catholic High School students gathered there to wait for their buses, a group of five Black Hebrew Israelites stood in a row “shouting scripture from red books” and taunting passers-by; as the students arrived they directed insults at them, including slurs, and they told Native American activists that the word Indian means “savage.” Nathan Phillips, a member of the Omaha tribe, said he stepped between the groups to defuse the tension. Short clips of Phillips and student Nicholas Sandmann went viral; a longer video released January 20 showed the preachers’ part, and outlets revised their reports.

The Washington Post identified the preachers as members of the House of Israel, a One West group led by Zabach, and wrote that they told the Native Americans they were descendants of the Israelite “Tribe of Gad” and called the white students “Edomites.” The same article named Israel United in Christ as “a related organization,” recently in the spotlight through Kendrick Lamar, and wrote that groups such as HOI are branded “hate groups” by the SPLC and the ADL. A news article on the Jersey City shooting, read in the class of December 27, 2019, again described the movement through its “role in a viral video confrontation at the Lincoln Memorial.”

points: The news called them “black” Hebrew Israelites to say they are not the real ones. The brother teaching at the Lincoln Memorial was Puerto Rican, and he was not shouting insults at the Native man: he was telling him he was from the tribe of Gad.

To start a campaign they dig up camps that talk like that, and the montage they showed of the Lincoln Memorial is another camp from years ago. That is not how a man of God talks: there is a way to speak about the people and condemn the evil they do, but they speak from the lust of their heart and make a bad name for the Israelite community.
teaching.quote: That's not how a man of God talks

answer.why: The classes’ rule for street preaching: “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” A man of God condemns evil without speaking from the lust of his heart.
“Ye shall know them by their fruits.” Each camp is known by its own conduct, not by another camp’s.
“Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations.” Israel made a byword on every screen is the curse foretold.

The class (Red Dragon Red Herring, December 27, 2019): the brother was not shouting insults at the Native man; he was telling him he was from the tribe of Gad.

events.title: The Jersey City shooting, and the coverage that tied it to the Israelites
events.summary: On December 10, 2019 David Anderson and Francine Graham killed a police detective and three people at a kosher grocery in Jersey City; because Anderson identified as a Black Hebrew Israelite, the coverage turned on the whole movement, though the attorney general said no formal link to any organization had been established.
account: On December 10, 2019 David N. Anderson and Francine Graham shot and killed Detective Joseph Seals at Bayview Cemetery, then killed the owner Mindy Ferencz, the employee Douglas Miguel Rodriguez and the customer Moshe Deutsch at the JC Kosher Supermarket in Jersey City, before police killed them after a shootout of more than three hours. They were also suspects in the December 7 murder of Michael Rumberger in Bayonne. New Jersey Attorney General Gurbir Grewal said the evidence pointed to acts of hate and domestic terrorism fueled by “hatred of the Jewish people and hatred of law enforcement.”

Anderson identified as a Black Hebrew Israelite and had posted hundreds of antisemitic and anti-police messages. Coverage turned on the movement as a whole. The SPLC’s Hatewatch wrote on December 12, 2019 that the suspects had “expressed interest” in Black Hebrew Israelites, and that month the SPLC listed 144 Black Hebrew Israelite organizations as hate groups. In a news article read in the class of December 27, 2019, the attorney general said that no formal links to that organization or to any other group had been established, and that the two were believed to have acted on their own.

points: After Representative Bass showed the report on Black identity extremists was false, a link was manufactured. The FBI and NYPD came and asked whether the man was a member of Israel United in Christ; they already knew he was not. He had visited another Israelite camp once, two years before, and IUIC had no school in Jersey City. They said it was a formality.

events.title: The Monsey stabbing, and the coverage that tied it to the Israelites
events.summary: On December 28, 2019 Grafton Thomas stabbed five people at a Hanukkah gathering in a rabbi’s home in Monsey; authorities said his journals referred to “Hebrew Israelites,” and coverage linked him to the movement, though his family’s lawyer said he belonged to no hate group and he had long been seriously mentally ill.
account: On the night of December 28, 2019, the seventh night of Hanukkah, a masked man with a large knife or machete entered the home of Rabbi Chaim Rottenberg in Monsey, New York and stabbed five Hasidic men; Rabbi Josef Neumann, 72, died of his wounds in March 2020. Grafton E. Thomas, 37, was arrested in Harlem that night. Authorities said his journals held antisemitic material and what appeared to be a reference to the Black Hebrew Israelites, stating that “Hebrew Israelites” have taken from “ebinoid Israelites.”

Thomas’s lawyer issued a statement for his family that he did not belong to any hate groups. He had a long history of serious mental illness and had been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2018; federal and state judges ruled him incompetent to stand trial. The attack was reported alongside Jersey City: a New York Post article read in the class described “the Black Hebrew Israelites, a secretive sect,” and said Thomas had attended a house of worship in East Harlem.

points: The Israelite community is not secretive: you can visit any Israelite school, and you don’t need a secret password. The paper’s reporter sat in on a sermon a whole year before and held it until the phone rang; the connections are manufactured, because you cannot blame an organization because someone attended somewhere. If they hold meetings about hatred in the community and accuse the Israelites, let the Israelites speak for themselves.
teaching.quote: You can't say because someone attended somewhere that the organization is to blame

answer.why: “Every man shall be put to death for his own sin.” The law does not lay one man’s crime on those he once sat among.
“Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked… who whet their tongue like a sword, and bend their bows to shoot their arrows, even bitter words.” It is the counsel against Israel that is secret.
“We found this fellow perverting the nation”: Christ was accused of what others did and planned.

events.title: Ebenezer Baptist seeks a restraining order against IUIC in Oklahoma City
events.summary: In June 2022 Ebenezer Baptist Church in Oklahoma City accused IUIC of harassing its members during the “Blitz the Christian Church” demonstrations and sought a restraining order; Judge Sheila Stinson ruled IUIC may demonstrate in the public right-of-way so long as it does not block traffic or keep members from the church.
account: Ebenezer Baptist Church, led by the Rev. Derrick Scobey, sought a temporary restraining order after a demonstration on June 12, 2022, accusing IUIC members of harassment, of “yelling and shouting rude, vile and obscene statements through a megaphone,” and of causing a car accident in which a church member was injured. Another pastor, the Rev. Kenneth Sherrill of Greater New Zion Baptist Church, called the demonstrations “an attack on our churches.” The Oklahoman introduced IUIC as “labeled a hate group by the Southern Poverty Law Center.”

Oklahoma County District Judge Sheila Stinson ruled that IUIC may demonstrate outside the church so long as its members stand in the public right-of-way, do not impede traffic and do not keep church members from coming and going. More than 50 IUIC members attended the hearing. Bishop Kani called the ruling a decisive victory and the request “frivolous,” and said the Blitz was telling Black congregations that Christianity was imposed on enslaved Africans and that the churches had failed to cure homelessness and broken families: “We don’t promote violence… they translate when we talk as hate because we’re trying to empower ourselves.”

points: When you truly live up to the testimony of Christ, you will be persecuted: taken to court, sued, some put to death. You must endure hardness as a good soldier. Our communities are destroyed, and somebody has to tell our people how to live, because what we have been doing is not working: the true prophets teach the commandments.

events.title: Kyrie Irving is suspended over Hebrews to Negroes
events.summary: On October 27, 2022 Brooklyn Nets star Kyrie Irving tweeted a link to Hebrews to Negroes: Wake Up Black America, a 2018 film promoting Black Hebrew Israelite beliefs; after it was condemned as antisemitic, the Nets suspended him without pay on November 3.
account: Hebrews to Negroes: Wake Up Black America, made by Ronald Dalton Jr. on a reported budget of $8,000 and released December 20, 2018, is based on Dalton’s book promoting Black Hebrew Israelite beliefs. Irving had first tweeted Black Hebrew Israelite doctrine in March 2021. On October 27, 2022 he tweeted a link to the film’s Amazon page.

The film was condemned as antisemitic: the ADL and other critics said it contained antisemitic tropes, Holocaust denial and fabricated quotations. Irving declined in two news conferences to apologize or disavow it, and on November 3, 2022 the Nets suspended him without pay; he then apologized and agreed to donate $500,000 to causes that combat hate. In November 2022 the ADL, the American Jewish Committee and the Jewish Federations of North America asked Amazon to stop distributing the book and film; Amazon declined.

points: They are coming down so hard on Kyrie because it is war: the dragon is wroth with the woman, the daughter of Zion, and makes war with the remnant of her seed which keep the commandments of God. A man is suspended without pay just for making a post. We must endure hardness as good soldiers and put on the whole armour of God.

events.title: An academic dictionary’s entry on Israel United in Christ
events.summary: On August 30, 2026 the Critical Dictionary of Apocalyptic and Millenarian Movements published Michael T. Miller’s entry on Israel United in Christ, which calls it the most populous Black Hebrew Israelite group and charges its teaching with conspiracy theory, selective misreading and an expectation of race war.
account: The entry, by Michael T. Miller in the Critical Dictionary of Apocalyptic and Millenarian Movements (edited by James Crossley and Alastair Lockhart), was published on August 30, 2026. It describes IUIC as the most populous group of the Black Hebrew Israelite movement and the most successful One West camp, with an estimated 10,000 members, led by Bishop Nathanyel Ben Israel.

It records charges in its own words: that IUIC’s eschatology predicts “the imminent ‘awakening’ of the true Israelites, followed by a race war and the enslavement/destruction of all non-Israelites”; that the group is a purveyor of “conspiracy theory in religion,” almost “conspiracy theory as religion”; that its history rests on “wild speculation” like a pseudohistory; and that “selective and seemingly deliberate misreading is also common.” It notes that IUIC, One West and Bishop Nathanyel “have been repeatedly accused of hatred, antisemitism, homophobia, conspiracy theories, and various other prejudices.”

The entry also records IUIC’s answer and its work: that IUIC “vociferously refute” the hate-group designation, open many videos with “We are not a hate group,” citing Romans 12:18, and tell members to notify the authorities of any plot to cause harm, citing Leviticus 5:1 and Romans 13:1. It writes that IUIC brings “a radically new message of race consciousness and dignity,” motivates people to improve their lives and commit to family, and does waste cleanup, youth and crisis support and prison outreach.

answer.why: IUIC’s own answer, as the entry records it: “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” No race war is taught by those who read this.
Cited by IUIC, as the entry records, for reporting any plot to harm anyone.

“After the way which they call heresy, so worship I the God of my fathers, believing all things which are written in the law and in the prophets.” Read in the classes against the names cult and heresy.
“As concerning this sect, we know that every where it is spoken against.” The apostles’ teaching was spoken against everywhere; the classes read it of themselves.

The ungodly say of the righteous: “He professeth to have the knowledge of God… He is grievous unto us even to behold… We are esteemed of him as counterfeits.” The ring: a people who call themselves the children of the Lord are charged with fantasy.
“A proverb, and a byword, among all nations”: the curse names the people’s story being made a byword.
